what: has_unpack_to_dest_fp32<> was defined TWICE verbatim, so ANY kernel including tilize_helpers.hpp failed to compile on TRISC (redefinition error). The tilize compute helper was unusable as shipped; this was my first hard failure and the error surfaced as a wall of JIT compile output rather than a clear duplicate-definition message. Removed the duplicate (no semantic change).
suggest: Keep the fix; add a compile smoke test that instantiates each kernel_lib compute helper once (a tiny kernel per header) so a duplicate/ill-formed helper cannot land green — every consumer of the header is blocked by it.

what: The doc presents ttnn.round_up, ttnn.div_up and ttnn.find_max_divisor as available python bindings (with examples and a summary table), and the generic_op template repeats them. None of the three exist in this build: following the doc produced AttributeError: module ttnn has no attribute round_up on the first device run. ttnn.tile_size / grid_to_cores / split_work_to_cores / get_dram_alignment DO exist, so the page is only partly accurate.
suggest: Verify each documented binding against the built module and mark the ones that are absent (or state the minimum commit that adds them), and stop recommending them in the descriptor template. A one-line note like "if round_up/div_up are missing in your build, define them locally" would have saved a failed run.

what: Both say scripts/run_safe_pytest.sh --profile emits generated/profiler/reports/<ts>/ops_perf_results*.csv and prints SAFE_PYTEST: PROFILER CSV: <path>. On this box the profiler clearly ran (Real-time profiler ... sync complete, frequency=1.349983 GHz) but NO reports dir and no CSV were ever produced, only the WARNING line - so the documented primary measurement path yielded nothing. I only got numbers after finding the in-process recipe in an examples test: set TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER=1 + TT_METAL_PROFILER_MID_RUN_DUMP=1 + TT_METAL_PROFILER_CPP_POST_PROCESS=1 BEFORE the device opens, then ttnn.ReadDeviceProfiler(device) + ttnn.get_latest_programs_perf_data() and read the DEVICE KERNEL DURATION [ns] analysis entry.
suggest: Document the in-process recipe as a first-class Layer-A option (it is strictly better for A/B arms: same session, no CSV parsing, per-arm attribution) and say what makes the --profile CSV path fail, e.g. whether it needs a device sync/readback in the test. Reference tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/examples/test_distribution_gate.py as the worked example.

what: The check requires a B0-set lever (B5/B7/...) to record measured.shape == the smallest shape in feature_spec.INPUTS. For tilize that shape is [1,1,30,32], which is a pad_mode=auto cell that the Phase-0 SUPPORTED rectangle correctly REFUSES - so at Phase 0 there is no honest way to satisfy the check: the op cannot run the shape at all, and running it via the private dispatch would read sticks past the end of the input buffer. Two blocking findings are therefore unavoidable at Phase 0 no matter how carefully the levers are measured, which trains an agent to either fudge measured.shape or ignore the checker.
suggest: Compare against the smallest INPUTS shape that the op currently SUPPORTS (the harness already knows SUPPORTED and can filter INPUTS through the same unsupported_reason() it uses for xfail), and fall back to the global smallest only when it is runnable. Otherwise let a row carry an explicit smallest_regime_blocked_by field naming the refusing axis, and downgrade the finding to signal.

what: No documented way to get the per-core L1 / CB budget from python, and ttnn.get_device_info is not exposed even though reports.cpp binds a DeviceInfo with worker_l1_size / cb_limit / l1_bank_size. The auto-fall-back-to-depth-1-rather-than-OOM rule (master.md C16, and this op prompt A6) needs exactly that number, so I had to guard the depth-2 decision with a hardcoded conservative constant - which is the kind of magic literal the same prompt tells me not to write.
suggest: Expose (or document) a python query for worker L1 size / cb_limit next to get_dram_alignment/get_l1_alignment, and say in the HAL Queries section which one to use for a CB-budget decision. The doc already forbids hardcoding 32/16/2048; the L1 budget deserves the same treatment.

what: The Blocking Model justifies TARGET_READ_BYTES=512 as the one-packet NoC fast path and cites NOC_MAX_BURST_SIZE=512 B, and the Mode-A ranking anchors its predicted targets on WH numbers (dram_peak 288 GB/s, 191 GB/s achievable, 88 us) - all stated without an arch caveat, while the run executed on Blackhole where NOC_MAX_BURST_SIZE is 256 words x 64 B = 16 KB and DRAM peak is ~448 GB/s. Measurement showed 512 B was 1.24x SLOWER than 1024 B on the square. The design did keep the knob sweepable and named the sweep as its own fallback, so this cost me only the sweep - but a reader could easily treat 512 B as a settled constant and never sweep it.
suggest: Stamp arch-derived constants and predicted targets with the arch they came from (as the perf examples do with a box/arch line), and phrase such a default as "512 B on WH; re-derive from NOC_MAX_BURST_SIZE and sweep on other parts" rather than as a property of the op.
